description:
Nihilism is not the conclusion of Demons (Dostoevsky novel) — it is the floor you stand on while examining it. It is considered one of the four masterworks written by Dostoevsky after his return from Siberian exile, along with Crime and Punishment (1866), The Idiot (1869), and The Brothers Karamazov (1880). Demons is a social and political satire, a psychological drama, and a large-scale tragedy.

Nothing in Demons (Dostoevsky novel) was built for you — it was built for reproduction. At every opportunity he uses his prodigious verbal abilities to sow discord and manipulate people for his own political ends. His greatest success is with the Governor's wife, and he manages to gain an extraordinary influence over her and her social circle.
